title: Windows 1.0发布 (图形界面的起步)
title_en: Release of Windows 1.0 (The Start of GUI)
city: 纽约 (赫尔姆斯利宫酒店)

summary.text: 1985年11月20日，在宣布整整两年后，微软终于发货了Windows 1.0。这并不是一个独立的操作系统，而是一个运行在MS-DOS之上的“操作环境”（Operating Environment）。面对苹果Macintosh的竞争，微软急需一个图形界面产品来保住其在PC市场的统治地位。Windows 1.0引入了下拉菜单、滚动条、图标和对话框，并支持鼠标操作。虽然它在当时因为运行缓慢、缺乏软件支持且界面简陋（窗口只能平铺，不能重叠）而遭到嘲笑，被称为“雾件”（Vaporware），但它标志着微软从命令行时代向图形界面时代迈出了艰难但关键的第一步。
summary.text_en: On November 20, 1985, two full years after its announcement, Microsoft finally shipped Windows 1.0. It was not a standalone operating system but an 'Operating Environment' running on top of MS-DOS. Facing competition from the Apple Macintosh, Microsoft desperately needed a GUI product to maintain its dominance in the PC market. Windows 1.0 introduced drop-down menus, scroll bars, icons, and dialog boxes, along with mouse support. Although it was mocked at the time for being slow, lacking software, and having a crude interface (windows could only be tiled, not overlapped) and was labeled 'Vaporware', it marked Microsoft's difficult but critical first step from the command line era to the GUI era.
key_points: 微软的第一个图形用户界面 (GUI) 产品
作为MS-DOS的扩展运行，而非独立系统
窗口采用“平铺” (Tiled) 布局，不可重叠
自带了记事本、画图、计算器和黑白棋游戏
确立了微软未来几十年的Windows产品线基础
key_points_en: Microsoft's first Graphical User Interface (GUI) product
Ran as an extension of MS-DOS, not an independent system
Windows used a 'Tiled' layout and could not overlap
Included Notepad, Paint, Calculator, and Reversi
Laid the foundation for Microsoft's Windows product line for decades to come

story.text: Windows 1.0的开发过程是一场漫长的噩梦。早在1983年，比尔·盖茨就在纽约的一场豪华发布会上宣布了它，并承诺1984年上市。然而，开发团队低估了在只有640KB内存的PC上运行图形界面的难度。项目一拖再拖，业内笑称它为“Vaporware”（雾件，指只闻其声不见其影的产品）。最初，这个项目被命名为“界面管理器”（Interface Manager），但营销天才罗兰·汉森说服盖茨改名为“Windows”，因为这更直观地描述了用户将在屏幕上看到的东西。为了避免被苹果起诉，微软还特意限制了功能，比如窗口不能重叠（虽然苹果后来还是起诉了，那是一场旷日持久的官司）。
story.text_en: The development of Windows 1.0 was a long nightmare. Bill Gates had announced it at a lavish event in New York back in 1983, promising a 1984 release. However, the team underestimated the difficulty of running a GUI on a PC with only 640KB of RAM. The project was delayed again and again, earning the industry nickname 'Vaporware'. Initially, the project was named 'Interface Manager', but marketing genius Rowland Hanson convinced Gates to rename it 'Windows' because it intuitively described what users would see. To avoid being sued by Apple, Microsoft intentionally limited features, such as preventing windows from overlapping (though Apple sued anyway in a protracted legal battle).

fun_facts.text: Windows 1.0内置了一个叫做《黑白棋》(Reversi) 的游戏。微软之所以加入它，并不是为了娱乐，而是为了教用户如何使用鼠标。通过下棋，用户可以练习“点击”和“拖拽”这些当时还很新鲜的操作。
fun_facts.text_en: Windows 1.0 included a game called Reversi. Microsoft included it not for fun, but to teach users how to use a mouse. By playing the game, users could practice 'clicking' and 'dragging', which were novel actions at the time.

fun_facts.text: 销售经理史蒂夫·鲍尔默（Steve Ballmer）为此拍摄了一段极其夸张的电视购物风格广告。他在广告中大喊大叫，像推销神奇拖把一样推销Windows，这段视频后来成为了互联网早期的鬼畜经典。
fun_facts.text_en: Sales manager Steve Ballmer filmed an incredibly exaggerated infomercial-style ad for it. He screamed and shouted, selling Windows like a miracle mop. This video later became a classic viral meme in the early internet era.

simple_explanation.text:
如果说DOS是让你在一个黑漆漆的房间里用打字机工作，Windows 1.0就是试图在这个房间里挂几幅画，开几扇窗。
虽然这扇窗户很简陋，打不开，风景也不好看，但它至少让原本枯燥的黑屏幕变得稍微生动了一点点。
它是为了不让苹果Mac独占风头而匆忙推出的“占位符”。
simple_explanation.text_en:
If DOS was working on a typewriter in a dark room, Windows 1.0 was an attempt to hang some pictures and open a few windows in that room.
Although the window was crude, stuck, and had a bad view, it at least made the boring black screen a little more lively.
It was a 'placeholder' rushed out to prevent the Apple Mac from stealing all the thunder.

applications.title: 画图 (MS Paint)
applications.text: 从Windows 1.0开始就存在的元老级应用，虽然功能简陋，但它让PC用户第一次体验到了用鼠标绘图的乐趣。
applications.text_en: A veteran app present since Windows 1.0. Though rudimentary, it gave PC users their first taste of drawing with a mouse.

applications.title: 记事本 (Notepad)
applications.text: 另一个伴随Windows 1.0诞生的应用。它证明了在图形界面下进行简单的文本编辑比在命令行里方便得多。
applications.text_en: Another app born with Windows 1.0. It proved that simple text editing was much easier in a GUI than in a command line.

impact.text: 从商业上看，Windows 1.0是失败的，销量惨淡且缺乏软件支持。但从历史长河看，它是决定性的。它开启的图形化道路，经过十年的迭代和打磨，最终在1995年爆发——**Windows 95** 的发布不仅引发了全球狂热，更彻底改变了人类使用电脑的方式。可以说，没有1.0艰难的“从0到1”，就没有后来Windows长达30年的全球垄断。
impact.text_en: Commercially, Windows 1.0 was a flop, with poor sales and little software support. But historically, it was decisive. The GUI path it opened, after a decade of iteration and polishing, finally exploded in 1995—the release of **Windows 95** not only sparked a global frenzy but fundamentally changed how humans use computers. It can be said that without the difficult '0 to 1' of version 1.0, there would be no 30-year global monopoly of Windows.

influenced_by.contribution: Macintosh（Mac的发布给微软造成了巨大的压力，迫使其加速推出图形界面产品）
influenced_by.contribution_en: Macintosh (The release of the Mac put immense pressure on Microsoft, forcing it to accelerate its GUI product)

influenced_by.contribution: MS-DOS（Windows 1.0是DOS的图形外壳，没有DOS它无法运行）
influenced_by.contribution_en: MS-DOS (Windows 1.0 was a graphical shell for DOS; it couldn't run without it)

influenced.contribution: 万维网（Windows最终为万维网的普及提供了最庞大的用户硬件载体，浏览器成为了Windows上的杀手级应用）
influenced.contribution_en: World Wide Web (Windows ultimately provided the massive hardware base for the Web's adoption; the browser became the killer app on Windows)

influence_chain.legacy_text: 它虽然丑陋，但它教会了全世界如何使用鼠标。
influence_chain.legacy_text_en: It was ugly, but it taught the world how to use a mouse.

quiz.question: Windows 1.0的窗口有什么独特的限制，与现在的Windows截然不同？
quiz.question_en: What unique limitation did Windows 1.0 windows have, making them very different from modern Windows?
options_en: Could only be tiled, not overlapped
quiz.explanation: 为了避免侵犯苹果的专利（或者是技术限制），Windows 1.0的窗口只能平铺（Tiled）在屏幕上，互不遮挡，而不能像现在这样随意重叠（Overlapping）。直到Windows 2.0才引入了重叠窗口。
quiz.explanation_en: To avoid infringing on Apple's patents (or due to technical limitations), windows in Windows 1.0 could only be tiled on the screen without covering each other, unlike the overlapping windows we have today. Overlapping windows were introduced in Windows 2.0.
